Design canvasUX.4 / UX.5 proposal2026-11-21

Tandem: listen first, then one kind of change at a time

A simpler guided flow for a time-poor person with a song idea, that loses no control. Three places instead of four: Sing, Your song, Share. After a take you hear it. Then each kind of change has a screen of its own, all with the same Play, Before / After and Put it back.

The current-flow frames are screenshots of the app at main (5b1c1c7), headless Chromium at 390 x 844 with a fake microphone. The proposed screens are drawings, not built. The written rationale, the control-by-control table and the roadmap split are in tandem-flow-redesign.md beside this file.

7Settings

  1. aA good screen that is in the wrong relation to the rest: how much pitch fixing is set here and again on the Notes step; the clean-up style only here; the beat style here and on Notes.
  2. bNothing on it can be heard. Each choice belongs beside the Before / After of the thing it changes; this screen should keep only what runs automatically.

8Show every control, on the phone: 4,031 px

  1. a4.8 screens. It is the desktop studio stacked, and it is the only place 102 of the studio's controls can be reached from: changing a chord, levels, takes, layers, the pitch-line editor, the recording options.
  2. bSo on a phone the choice today is four long guided pages or this. The change views are the missing middle.

Frame BThe proposed flow, as a map

A hub with spokes, not a longer wizard. The steps of making a song depend on each other (a new key changes the chords, a note edit changes what pitch fixing aims at), so people go back and forth; a strict line of nine screens would fight that. The line that does exist is short: sing, hear it, share it.

1. Every screen that changes sound has Play on itIn the same place, doing the obvious thing for that screen.
2. One kind of change on a screenIts two or three everyday controls in view; the rest behind one More.
3. Always a way backBefore / After and Put it back in every change view; Undo everywhere; a new take never replaces an old one.
4. The same controls underneathEach view is the studio's own controls moved in, as the guided view does today. Show every control is unchanged.

Frame DHow the desktop studio relates

Frame EWhat is borrowed, and from where

Apps that make complicated work feel like a few plain steps without removing the power. Each card says what the app does, what Tandem takes from it and what it leaves. Where a behaviour could not be confirmed from a source it is said so.

Music app for non-musicians

Voloco

Record→Edit view opens→change effect, key

When you stop recording, the Edit view appears by itself. Effects are processing on top of the recording, not baked in: you can change the effect later, or even after exporting, without singing again.

Borrowed: Stop leads straight to a screen about the take you just made (Your take). The take is never altered: clean-up and pitch fixing are things laid over it that can be changed or taken off (Voice view, Before / After).

Not copied: Presets named after artists and styles. Tandem's person wants their own tune to sound right, not an effect.

Source: Voloco help: Understanding vocal effects · How to use vocal presets
One tool open at a time

Instagram photo editor

AdjustBrightnessContrastWarmthCancelDone

A row of named tools. Tapping one opens only its slider; Done keeps it. A grey dot appears under every tool that has been used, so you can see at a glance what was changed.

Borrowed: The hub of named kinds of change, one open at a time, Done to come back, and the dot on a tile that has been used. Put it back is the Cancel.

Not copied: Filters first. Tandem has no one-tap look for a song; the nearest thing, Genre, sits in Sound.

Source: Instagram Help Centre: edit photos · Instagram: introducing creative tools
Phone editor with a bottom tool bar

CapCut

AudioTextEffectsSpeedDone

The bottom bar shows only the tools that fit what is selected; a tool takes over the lower part of the screen and a tick confirms it, while the preview keeps playing above.

Borrowed: The fixed frame of every change view: the player on top always, the tool below, one way out. Tiles that do not apply are left out (no Band on the web, Pitch help hidden for a beat take).

Not copied: A reviewer found the tool labels in very fine print. Tandem's kinds are words in full-size tiles, not icons with captions, and there is no sideways-scrolling bar of twelve.

Source: Hollyland: how to use CapCut · TechRadar review
Edit panels by kind, hold to compare

Lightroom for mobile

LightColorEffectsDetailhold: Before

Edits are grouped into panels by kind. Pressing and holding the photo shows the original with a Before label; letting go returns to the edit. People have asked Adobe for a before / after of only the current change, which the phone app does not have.

Borrowed: Before / After one touch away in every view. Tandem's is scoped to the view you are in (the thing Lightroom's users ask for), because the snapshot taken on opening a view is free with the undo history.

Not copied: Press-and-hold. A phrase of music takes seconds to judge, so it is a switch that stays where you put it.

Source: Adobe: gestures in Lightroom for mobile · Adobe community: before / after of the current change only
Nothing is destructive

Apple Photos, Edit

CancelAdjustFiltersCropDone

Edit opens three kinds of change. Done keeps them; Cancel, then Discard Changes, drops them. Edits can be changed or removed later because the original is kept.

Borrowed: Put it back for one view's changes, and the promise that the take is always still there. It matches the product principle: never silently overwrite a recording.

Not copied: A tap-on-the-photo compare could not be confirmed from Apple's guide, so it is not claimed here.

Source: Apple: iPhone User Guide, edit photos · How-To Geek: editing in Photos
A long job as an interview

TurboTax

one step→plain English→review

A prescriptive flow that puts one step in front of the person at a time, in plain English, with a line on why each thing is asked, built on research that people wanted to feel the product had their back.

Borrowed: Plain words everywhere, "What Tandem did" after a take, one suggested next tile, and a review on Share ("In your song") with a Change link per line. The review-with-links screen is from knowing the product, not from the sources found.

Not copied: The forced order. A tax return has one; a song does not (see the next card).

Source: Appcues: how TurboTax makes a dreadful experience delightful · Fast Company: how TurboTax used design
The reason for a hub

Nielsen Norman Group on wizards

step→step→steponly if steps are independent

Showing a few options a step (staged disclosure) works when the steps have little to do with each other, and is a problem when they depend on each other and people must go back and forth. Putting rarely used features on a second screen (progressive disclosure) makes an app easier to learn and less error-prone.

Borrowed: The shape of the whole proposal: a short line (sing, hear, share) around a hub, with Prev / Next as a convenience between views and not as the only road. One More fold a view for the expert controls.

Source: NN/g: progressive disclosure · NN/g: wizards
Pitch fixing as an effect with an amount

BandLab

record→AutoPitchkeyintensity

Record the vocal, then apply AutoPitch and set the key and the intensity. The key can be found from what was recorded.

Borrowed: Voice view: Fix my singing is one button and a How much slider, with the key found from the tune; the rest is under More.

Not copied: The mixing desk as the home screen. BandLab opens on tracks; Tandem's person has one tune.

Source: BandLab: AutoPitch · BandLab help: using AutoPitch
A simple view over a full one

GarageBand for iPhone

Touch Instrument↔Tracks view

You can move, trim, cut, loop or split a region inside the instrument without switching to Tracks view. Undo covers recording and changing the sound as well as edits.

Borrowed: The guided view and Show every control are two views of one song with one undo history, and the simple one borrows the full one's real controls. Already Tandem's architecture; the proposal leans on it harder.

Not copied: Live Loops and the instrument browser: more to learn before the first sound.

Source: Apple: edit regions in GarageBand for iPhone · Apple: edit notes in regions
A mixer anyone can read

Moises

Vocals ▬▬▬Drums ▬▬Bass ▬▬▬

After separating a song, each part is a row with its own volume and mute; export is a part at a time or the whole mix.

Borrowed: Sound view: one row a part with what plays it, how loud and on or off, in place of mute / solo / dB strips.

Source: Moises: how to separate audio tracks · Moises on the App Store

Looked at and left out: Duolingo's one-task screens fit drills (Tandem's Practise already works that way) but not open-ended editing; Suno and other prompt-to-song apps make the song for you, which is the opposite of keeping the person's idea central; Canva and Splice are template and loop libraries, and Tandem has neither. These three judgements are from knowing the apps, not from sources read for this review.
